title: Propositional logic: formulas, truth tables, and consequence
summary: Finite formulas, truth-value assignments, substitution, and truth tables that decide consequence and produce counterexamples.
abstract: If rain always makes a path wet, and it rains, the path must be wet; a wet path alone does not establish rain. Propositional logic makes this difference precise by studying formulas built from statements using “and,” “or,” “not,” and “if.” Assigning truth or falsity to their basic statements determines the truth of the whole formula. Replacing those basic statements consistently by other formulas preserves every valid inference. For finitely many premises and a conclusion, a finite truth table decides whether the conclusion follows, and a failing row gives an explicit assignment showing why it does not.

based_on.title: Sets, Logic, Computation: An Open Introduction to Metalogic (Fall 2025; remix 38828e6, Text 0c1e9e3)
based_on.pages: 92–95 (§6.3, propositional formation clauses, abbreviations, and induction)
